details.description: Llama 3 8B is Meta's smallest base, pretrained (not instruction-tuned) language model in the Llama 3 family, released April 18, 2024. Meta pretrained it on over 15 trillion tokens of publicly available data with an optimized transformer architecture and grouped-query attention, giving it an 8,192-token context window and a knowledge cutoff of March 2023. As a base model it produces free-form text continuations rather than following chat instructions, and Meta positions it mainly as a starting point for further fine-tuning rather than for direct assistant use.
advantages: Scores 66.6 on MMLU and 72.6 on CommonSenseQA as the pretrained (base) 8B model, per Meta's official Llama 3 model card.
Pretrained on over 15 trillion tokens of data, about seven times the training data Meta used for Llama 2, per Meta's Llama 3 launch post.
disadvantages: Is a base, non-instruction-tuned checkpoint, so it is not optimized for chat or assistant-style interaction the way the Instruct version is.
Context window is limited to 8,192 tokens, far short of the 128,000-token window Meta introduced with the later Llama 3.1 family.
Meta's model card states intended use is commercial and research use in English; using it in other languages requires developers to fine-tune and safety-test it themselves.
use_cases: Serving as a base checkpoint for supervised fine-tuning or RLHF into custom chat or assistant models
General-purpose natural language generation and text completion tasks
Research and benchmarking of base (pre-alignment) language model capabilities

notes: Bud's catalog serves this base model over /v1/chat/completions, but Meta's own model card describes the un-suffixed 8B checkpoint as the pretrained/base model, distinct from the Instruct version (covered separately as llama-v3-8b-instruct-hf). Benchmarked as a base model accordingly.
